security_audit.summary: Most backtick, reconnaissance, and entropy alerts are Markdown or ordinary Chinese text. The skill directs execution of an unpinned npm package that handles credentials, and its optional download workflow accepts remote URLs and suggests a fixed proxy. No evidence of an attempt to override this audit was found.

remediation.issue: Authentication, research, and downloads use a mutable npm release.
remediation.suggestion: Use an approved CLI pinned to an exact version and verified integrity hash. Require consent before installing or running it.

remediation.issue: The CLI handles credentials from the environment or a persistent JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a scoped key from a secret manager. Verify owner-only file permissions and ensure diagnostics and logs never reveal secrets.

remediation.issue: Shell examples leave argument handling implicit.
remediation.suggestion: Pass validated inputs as separate arguments without invoking a shell. Apply this rule to research inputs, media URLs, and output paths.

remediation.issue: Media downloads accept remote URLs and suggest a fixed local proxy.
remediation.suggestion: Validate download and redirect destinations against approved public media hosts. Use only a user-approved proxy and confine writes to the approved directory.

remediation.issue: Billing instructions can relay a link supplied by an API error.
remediation.suggestion: Use the fixed provider billing page rather than links returned in errors. Leave any payment to the user.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Inputs in Shell Command Templates
semantic_findings.description: The examples put research inputs, returned media URLs, and output paths into shell templates. Direct substitution can let those values change the command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow favors direct shell execution and shows no argument isolation. Actual injection would depend on how the host constructs the invocation.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Destinations for Media Downloads
semantic_findings.description: The workflow passes provider-returned media URLs directly to a local downloader. Without destination checks, a bad URL or redirect could reach a private service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly preserves and fetches returned URLs without describing validation. The external downloader might enforce restrictions not shown in the skill.

semantic_findings.title: Billing Links Taken From API Errors
semantic_findings.description: The workflow prefers a billing link returned in an error over a fixed fallback. It does not require verifying the link before showing it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text calls for an official link but does not specify how to verify it. A misleading error could direct the user to phishing.

content.user_title: Research X Posts and Account Replies
content.value_statement: It is hard to tell what an account says from what others say in its comments. Use SocialDataX to sample posts and outgoing replies, then report findings with source links.
actual_capabilities: Search X posts by keyword through SocialDataX.
Look up an X profile by username, account ID, or profile URL.
List posts published by an account and group them by topic.
List replies written by an account separately from comments it receives.
Summarize representative evidence with original links, timestamps, and available engagement signals.
Save returned media through the CLI when the user requests a download.
limitations: Research queries require a SocialDataX credential for the CLI or an authenticated hosted MCP connection.
Requests can consume credits, and results may be partial or omit fields.
A limited sample does not establish platform-wide trends, complete account activity, or private views.
The skill does not post, like, comment, or change an X account. Optional CLI downloads write files locally.

use_cases.title: Find angles for an article
use_cases.description: Sample posts about a topic and identify recurring questions with representative links.

use_cases.title: Compare competitor messaging
use_cases.description: Review a bounded sample from two accounts and compare their topics and content formats.

use_cases.title: Review how an account joins discussions
use_cases.description: Group an account's outgoing replies by topic and separate direct statements from interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Find posts on a topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Search X for [topic]. Review one page and summarize common themes with links to representative posts.

prompt_templates.title: Review an account's posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up [account] and review the first page of its posts. Group the posts by topic and include dates and source links where available.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an account's replies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review replies written by [account], not comments on its posts. Group them by topic and distinguish direct quotes from your observations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two accounts within a sample limit
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the posts and outgoing replies of [account A] and [account B]. Use up to two pages per list and report gaps before drawing conclusions.

output_examples.input: Search X for heat pump installation and summarize one page.
output: Illustrative sample: eight posts from the first results page.
Two recurring questions concerned installation costs and performance in cold weather.
A live report would link to representative posts. This sample does not establish a wider trend.

output_examples.input: Summarize the discussions a selected account joined.
output: Illustrative sample: six outgoing replies. Comments received by the account are excluded.
Four replies addressed repair questions, and two discussed delivery.
Some timestamps were unavailable. The sample does not establish how often the account responds.

best_practices: Set a page or item limit before comparing accounts.
Keep original post links and timestamps, and label missing fields.
Use a reviewed CLI release or an approved hosted MCP connection, and keep API keys out of chat.
anti_patterns: Treating comments an account receives as replies it wrote.
Claiming a few results represent the entire platform.
Automatically restarting a partial query from the first page.

faq.question: What access do I need?
faq.answer: Research requires a SocialDataX API key for the direct CLI or an authenticated hosted MCP connection. Keep the key out of chat.

faq.question: How can I identify an account?
faq.answer: Provide an X username, account ID, or profile URL.

faq.question: Are replies and comments the same?
faq.answer: Replies here are messages the account wrote. Comments on a post are messages other users may have sent to that post.

faq.question: Will this change my X account?
faq.answer: No. It does not post, like, comment, or modify an X account.

faq.question: What happens if results are partial or credits run out?
faq.answer: The skill preserves results already retrieved. It can resume within the original limits when the issue is resolved and a continuation token is available.

faq.question: Can I save media from a result?
faq.answer: The CLI can save media on request when a usable URL is available. Downloads write to a local directory.
